parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the ESM, .mjs, /output, no external dependency, no Python command, manual argv parsing, and exact stdout/stderr/exit-code requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership while launching one broad workflow to probe semantics. The workflow itself split into five initial probe agents, a critic, and twelve follow-up probes.
parallel.implementation: The parent built a multi-module JS port under /output with argparse, bidict, traceback, sys, repr, number, and unicode helpers, then patched parser and output semantics after local diffs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact contained test19.mjs plus lib/collections, lib/argparse, lib/python, and lib/bidict modules. No child wrote the submitted /output implementation.
parallel.verification: The parent ran sample probes, a 118-case diff matrix from two working directories, and a large randomized fuzzer, but the workflow aggregate never returned and the final 2500-case fuzzer was killed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation completed at 145/157, matching the serial score. The observable parallel-specific unfinished work is the killed workflow aggregate and killed final fuzzer, not a proven unique hidden-case implementation defect.

serial.requirements: The serial agent had the same task prompt and recognized the ESM, .mjs, /output, no external dependency, manual argv parsing, and exact observable behavior requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial run used one actor for probing, implementation, integration, and verification; status records workflows and delegation tools disabled.
serial.implementation: The serial agent built a multi-module JS port under /output with pyruntime, argparse, and bidict libraries, then refactored modules while preserving local behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact contained test19.mjs plus lib/pyruntime, lib/argparse, and lib/bidict modules, with import and forbidden API audits done before timeout.
serial.verification: The serial run returned 783/783 differential matches from /workspace and from the dataset cwd, then returned 500/500, 400/400, and final 300/300 random fuzz matches before closure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite strong local verification, the official evaluator still failed 12 of 157 samples. The logs do not expose which hidden cases caused the remaining shared gap.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel saw the same prompt requiring pure ESM Node.js, .mjs files, manual process.argv parsing, exact output, /output delivery, no external packages, and no Python execution.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial saw the byte-identical task prompt and worked against the same executable and constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no material requirement-recognition difference; both attempts targeted the same broad behavioral surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split semantic probing into a workflow while the parent retained the implementation and local test work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had workflows disabled and no delegation, so the sole agent owned probing, implementation, integration, and delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run added a broad child-probe layer; serial kept the same work in one context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were explicit about the executable, no Python, the source skeleton, and exact stdout/stderr matching, but the resulting workflow aggregate did not return to the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept findings, patches, and verification results in the same trajectory, avoiding a parent-child result interface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The issue was not an incomplete child brief or interface contract; it was that the workflow result boundary remained unresolved under budget pressure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented test19.mjs plus argparse, bidict, and Python-like runtime helpers under lib/collections, lib/argparse, lib/python, and lib/bidict.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a similar multi-module port under lib/pyruntime, lib/argparse, and lib/bidict.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The file layouts differ, but both delivered a substantial JS runtime approximation and the same official score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel's TaskOutput call timed out while the workflow still reported running, and the workflow state later recorded status killed with result null.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verifier commands returned directly into the only agent context, including deterministic and random differential-test success reports.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the aggregate workflow verifier result; serial retained and consumed its verification results before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel submitted a coherent /output artifact, and child agents were probe-only actors rather than concurrent writers of the deliverable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial submitted a coherent /output artifact from the sole agent, with no delegation and no shared-workspace race.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete shared-state collision distinguishes the pair; the difference is workflow lifecycle and budget, not write ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel achieved a 118/118 matrix locally and attempted a broad fuzzer, but the workflow aggregate did not return and the last large fuzzer ended with exit code 137.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial returned 783/783 comparisons, 500/500 and 400/400 fuzz checks, then after refactor returned 783/783 plus 300/300.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had more completed in-context verification evidence; parallel's late verifier workflow and final fuzzer were unfinished, though official scores matched.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used one workflow, 18 child logs, 871105 child tokens, and then the main process timed out with return code 143.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out with return code 143, but it had no delegation and no child workflow consuming separate budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both hit the cell deadline, but only the parallel run spent substantial budget on an unfinished fan-out workflow and a killed final fuzzer.

outcome_analysis.explanation: This pair is not discordant. The current completed status.json evaluations show both modes failed with exactly 145 of 157 samples passed. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level: the parallel run spent substantial budget on a broad verifier workflow whose aggregate result never returned, while the serial run kept verification local and returned its differential-test results. That difference did not translate into a different official outcome.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out consumed deadline and token budget, left the aggregate verifier result unavailable, and coincided with the final fuzzer being killed.
The parent still produced and submitted a coherent artifact, so the retained pattern is adverse process evidence rather than a proven unique implementation root cause.
serial_contributors: Serial used no child agents and received its deterministic and fuzz verification outputs directly in the sole agent context.
Serial nevertheless failed the same 12 official cases as parallel, so its local verification also missed hidden evaluator behavior.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two implementations used different module layouts and helper names but converged to the same official score.
The remaining official failures are shared hidden-case gaps not exposed by the logged local harnesses.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator completed successfully in both modes and reported identical 145/157 scores.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel parent launched a broad verifier workflow and continued local work while it ran. The workflow expanded to 18 child agents and consumed large child-token and tool-call budget; it ended killed with result null, and the parent's TaskOutput call received only a running-timeout status before the final local fuzzer was killed. Serial kept equivalent verification in one context and received completed verifier results.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parallel verifier workflow never returned an aggregate result and the parent lost closure budget, ending with a killed final fuzzer rather than a completed final verification loop.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: A verifier result failed to return, but the directly corrective boundary is reducing or staging the broad fan-out; treating the absent aggregate as Missing Verifier Return would double-count the same chain.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Missing Verifier Return was suppressed because the missing aggregate is downstream of the retained fan-out budget episode.
Early Child Termination was suppressed because workflow kill was part of overall deadline closure, not a separate parent cancellation episode.
Blind Timeout Wait was suppressed because the parent inspected TaskOutput and then continued local work.
Critical-Path Starvation and Oversized Child Task were suppressed because the evidence is collective fan-out breadth, not generic underallocation or one oversized child.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the fan-out budget episode clears the paired retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The retained pattern has unique anchors and consequence; downstream timeout, missing return, and child-progress symptoms are not duplicated as separate labels.
